_readme: THE AUDIODEX SCENE (2026-10-15, round two; Jon: two phones side by side, as few words as possible). One word typed into both phones at once: Voice Memos (left) finds nothing, AudioDex (right) finds the memo and the song it became. The memo is REAL (Jon's pick): the first 18 s of public/listen/thanksgiving-a-capella.mp3 are the raw voice memo his family sent from a Thanksgiving dinner he couldn't attend; the clip is cut to public/archive/thanksgiving.m4a. The word 'thanksgiving' is never said in it, so a transcript search cannot find it; AudioDex names it. 'lines' are Whisper's own segments (large-v3-turbo, start/end seconds), every one it heard; '♪' marks the sung note; 'Jonny' is Jon's spelling; 'note' is the sung note measured from 1.5-5.0 s (215 Hz, an A a little flat). 'peaks' = RMS of the 18 s in 64 bins. 'rows' pair each stock name with the name AudioDex gave the same file (art, no real names). The date is the manifest's year's Thanksgiving. 'tapeAt': the second the cassette starts from when pressed (Jon: a few seconds already heard, then the door, then the song).

Maybe there's something you can use.
